sources.topic: Bounded BYTE buffers, type tags, big-endian numeric examples, string length/NUL/end markers, advancing index, named scalars and event bounds

contract.buffers: One-dimensional BYTE ARRAY references, 1..244 bytes; disjoint index/status; complete prepared item/marker writes preserve unused data and unknown tails
contract.encoding: Big-endian tags 16/17/209, signed INTEGER32 and finite REAL32, one-byte ASCII text length plus NUL, two-byte zero end marker; returned index points at marker
contract.named_data: INTEGER/REAL/STRING leaves of explicit current/attached program roots and static paths; blank owner uses executing module; system paths excluded
contract.send_capture: Read-only typed independent buffer captured once before later output selectors; no accidental buffer-parameter write effect
contract.typed_mode: Validate common envelope and publish used prefix through its marker; unused unknown tails ignored
contract.raw_mode: Publish the complete fully initialized buffer unchanged; no custom-format decoding
contract.outbox: Explicit PcExchange with event 0..255, bounded queue, monotonic publication sequence and detached host drain; event-only data is null
contract.persistence: Checked format/capacity/history, ordered messages and bounded packet hex; no callback or executable consumer restored

boundaries: No GEMM/PC transport, callbacks, delivery, controller timing or native status equivalence
Typed send validation and used-prefix publishing are chosen offline policies; arbitrary protocols require raw mode
Direct argument/type/protection errors may raise before status writes; strict mode deferred
